analyst.summary: Apollo Hospitals had a strong FY26 -- revenue up 16% to Rs 25,229 cr and profit up 34% to Rs 1,942 cr -- with its core hospital business showing healthy occupancy (68%) and rising realizations (ARPOB +9%), and its long-loss-making pharmacy-and-digital arm (Apollo 24/7) finally turning solidly profitable. The company is self-funding a large new-bed expansion that will pressure margins modestly through FY27 before paying off in FY28, and a long-planned demerger of the pharmacy/digital business is still working through regulatory approvals. Against this genuinely improving business, however, the stock trades at roughly 65 times trailing earnings, a price that already assumes a much faster and longer growth run than we think is realistic, alongside a pending Supreme Court matter over a flagship Delhi hospital's charity-care obligations. We rate it a Hold: a good, improving business, but not one offering value at the current price.
